chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ibrahim, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Takbir of the Days of Tashriq is from the Dhuhr prayer - from the Day of Sacrifice until the Fajr prayer of the Days of Tashriq, if you stay in Mina; and if you leave Mina, there is no Takbir upon you. And the Takbir is: 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, La ilaha illa Allah, wa Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, wa lillah al-hamd. Allahu Akbar 'ala ma hadana, wa Allahu Akbar 'ala ma razaqana min bahimati al-an'am, wa al-hamd lillah 'ala ma ablanah.'

key_terms.أَيَّامِ التَّشْرِيقِ: Days of Tashriq (the 11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct time and text for the Takbir during the Days of Tashriq in Mina?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* specifies the ritual timing and formula for the Takbir during the Days of Tashriq, linking the glorification directly to the sacrifice of livestock. It highlights the Shia scholarly distinction that the obligation to recite Takbir is contingent upon remaining in Mina; once the pilgrim departs, the specific ritual recitation concludes. The text emphasizes gratitude for divine guidance and sustenance, reflecting the spiritual dimension of the Hajj rites beyond mere physical action.
